queries.details: Extract asset or holding-level financial data only from financial or investment statements. Do not create financial statement results from tax forms such as 1099-INT, 1099-DIV, 1099-B, W-2, or IRS forms. Do not create financial statement results from life insurance or annuity policy statements. Create one result only for a specific named security, investment, fund, property holding, account, or cash balance shown in detailed holding-level sections such as Investment Detail, Holdings, Positions, Schedule of Investments, or Portfolio Holdings. Do not create results from Asset Composition, Overview, Allocation, Summary, Change in Account Value, account total, asset-class total, or category-level rows. Generic labels such as Fixed Income, Equities, Bond Funds, Equity Funds, ETFs, Other Assets, Total Assets, or Total Account Value are summary categories, not account names. Use exact values shown. Treat fair value, market value, current value, investment value, holdings value, cash balance, or account value as asset values only when tied to a specific named holding, security, fund, account, or cash balance. If the same asset value appears in multiple sections, extract it once using the most detailed holding-level row. Do not duplicate summary, total, or repeated statement values. Leave blank if not shown.

entities.criteria: Name of the specific named account, investment, security, fund, or property holding tied to the asset value. Look across Schedule of Investments, holding tables, and statement headers for the named entity. When a row has a labeled Account Name, Account Title, or Account Holder field, use that value and do not use Management Strategy, Model, Allocation, or Benchmark fields as the account name. Do not return asset category or line-item labels. Return Null if no named entity is shown.
data_validation_rules: Do not use owner, annuitant, insured, client, or taxpayer names as the account name unless the document explicitly labels that person’s name as the account/investment name.
Do not use Management Strategy, Model, Allocation, or Benchmark fields as the account name.

If a holding name is followed by a ticker, symbol, CUSIP, or security identifier after a colon, return only the holding name as the Account Name. Remove only the identifier text, not nearby descriptive holding-name lines.

For securities with wrapped description lines, do not stop at the first line; combine descriptive lines that describe the same holding, even if a SYMBOL or CUSIP line appears between them, but exclude the identifier/rating text itself. For equities or ADRs, include unlabeled wrapped share-description lines, such as “1 NEW YORK SH REP 1 ORD,” even when they appear after a SYMBOL line.

entities.criteria: Type or classification of the account, investment, asset, or holding as shown in the document. Preserve bracketed or parenthetical qualifiers shown in the section header or label, such as “[Non-Sweep].” When a combined section header contains multiple types, use the more specific row or subsection label as the Account Type. Do not shorten combined terms such as “Cash and cash equivalents” or “529 Education Savings.” Examples may include brokerage, IRA, trust, 401(k), 529 education savings, cash and cash equivalents, margin, equity, bond, mutual fund, ETF, annuity, real estate entity, fund, or security.
data_validation_rules: Use the most specific row or subsection label directly tied to the holding; Do not use broad parent headers such as “Investment Detail — Fixed Income” when a more specific type such as “US Treasuries,” “Corporate Bonds,” or “Municipal Bonds” is shown.

entities.criteria: Security ticker symbol only.
CUSIP only.
ISIN only.
Number of units, shares, or contracts held.

Current market price per unit or share. Use values from Market Price, Price, or Current Price fields only. Do not use Cost Per Unit, Cost Per Share, purchase price, or acquisition cost as Price. If Market Price is N/A or not shown, return Null.

Current value of the asset, holding, investment, security, account, or cash balance. Include fair value, market value, current value, holdings value, cash balance, account value, total assets, or total investments only when clearly labeled as asset-related. Do not use equity, members’ capital, partner capital, liabilities, contributions, income/loss, expenses, or operating activity amounts as asset values.

Cost basis shown for the holding, investment, security, account, or asset. Extract the purchase/acquisition basis from fields labeled Cost Basis, Total Cost Basis, or lot-level Cost Basis tied to the same holding. Do not use Adjusted Cost Basis as Cost Basis when a separate Cost Basis or Total Cost Basis is shown. If only Adjusted Cost Basis is shown and no Cost Basis is available for that holding, return the adjusted value.

Gain or loss value explicitly labeled or shown for the holding, investment, security, account, or asset, such as realized gain/loss, unrealized gain/loss, unrealized appreciation/depreciation, or change in fair value. Do not calculate gain/loss from Asset Value and Cost Basis. Return Null if no gain/loss value is explicitly shown.

queries.details: Extract insurance or annuity statement data. Use exact values shown. Leave blank if not shown. Create one result per unique Asset Name + Type of Funds combination, not per page, section, table, or repeated appearance. For life insurance or annuity statements, capture displayed policy accounts, subaccounts, fixed accounts, loan accounts, indexed accounts, and annuity fund/account lines as Type of Funds. Do not skip displayed policy accounts, subaccounts, fixed accounts, loan accounts, indexed accounts, or annuity fund/account lines with $0.00 values. If the same fund/account appears in multiple sections or pages, merge its information into one result and return only one output row for that fund/account. Repeat policy-level values, such as surrender charge, total value, policy loan, and surrender value, across all fund/account entries under the same policy when they apply to the entire policy. For whole life policies, capture Policy Loan and Surrender Value when present. Do not create separate entries from insurer, carrier, institution, brand, logo names, coverage, rider, face amount, death benefit lines, policy numbers, contract numbers, or account numbers. Merge them under the same policy/product and fund/account.

entities.criteria: Name of the policy, contract, holding, or fund exactly as shown. For life insurance policies, use the overall policy/product name as the Asset Name, not policy numbers, contract numbers, account numbers, policy account names, subaccounts, fixed accounts, loan accounts, indexed account names, coverage names, rider names, face amount labels, insurer names, carrier names, institution names, or brand names. Include qualifiers such as Non Qualified, Qualified, IRA, or Roth IRA when they appear as part of the displayed name. Do not append or return policy, contract, or account numbers unless they are explicitly part of the displayed asset name.
data_validation_rules: Exclude product-type wording already captured in Asset Type, such as “Indexed Universal Life Insurance."

entities.criteria: Insurance carrier or institution name.
data_validation_rules: Return one name only: the full legal carrier/company name when shown. Treat shortened names, brand names, logos, and aliases as the same carrier and exclude them. Example: If both “Pacific Life” and “Pacific Life Insurance Company” appear, return only “Pacific Life Insurance Company.”

entities.criteria: Product type as shown, such as whole life, universal life, annuity, variable annuity, individual annuity, or MYGA. For life insurance, return only the most specific product type shown, e.g., Indexed Universal Life Insurance instead of Universal Life. For annuity policies, return both the parent annuity type and specific subtype when shown. Do not include adjustment features unless part of the product name.

Fund type, subaccount, allocation name, policy account, or funding/tax classification such as Qualified, Non Qualified, IRA, or Roth IRA. For life insurance policies, return policy account names such as Fixed Account or Loan Account, not as Asset Name. For annuities, do not use product terms such as 5 Year MYGA as the fund type.
Year the funds become available, mature, or can be accessed without restriction, only if explicitly shown; Do not calculate or infer.

Value of the holding, fund, subaccount, or annuity accumulation value. For annuities, use Ending Accumulation Value when shown. Do not use face amounts, death benefit amounts, coverage amounts, rider amounts, premiums, or loan availability amounts as Holdings Value.
Value explicitly labeled cash balance or cash value.
Separate surrender charge amount only. If no separate charge amount is shown, leave blank.
How far along the surrender schedule the policy is, such as schedule year, years remaining, or surrender period end date.
Margin or debit balance shown, if any.

Total account value, contract value, policy value, or annuity accumulation value. For annuity statements, use Ending Accumulation Value or final Accumulation Value when shown. Do not use surrender value as total value.
Outstanding policy loan balance. Use for whole life when shown.
Cash surrender value, net surrender value, or ending cash surrender value. Use for life insurance or annuity statements when shown.

queries.details: Extract bank statement transaction records from bank statements, including cash, bank sweep, deposits/withdrawals, bank interest, and fees/charges activity such as checks, Visa/card purchases, BANK CREDIT FROM BROKERAGE, BANK TRANSFER TO BROKERAGE, BANK INTEREST/BANK INT, and actual service/advisory fees. Create one result per posted transaction, and repeat the bank name, account holder name, account number, and statement period for each transaction to identify the source account. A valid transaction must have its own transaction, posted, process, or settle date; exclude Cash Transactions Summary category rows such as “Withdrawals and Other Debits” and “Fees and Charges. Do not extract summary totals, balances, disclosures, or fee-waiver messages as transactions, but include actual fee/charge transactions. Do not create transactions from summary balances, but use the most specific source-account balance for the transaction: for Bank Sweep, BANK INTEREST, or BANK INT activity, use Bank Sweep Opening Balance and Ending Balance; otherwise use Starting Cash and Ending Cash when no transaction-level running balance is shown. Exclude investment-only activity such as buys, sells, dividends for reinvestment, and reinvested shares. Exclude security/fund income such as money market fund dividends and Treasury/bond interest; Include only interest explicitly tied to bank or sweep activity. Use exact values shown. Leave blank if not shown.

entities.criteria: Name of the bank or financial institution issuing the statement. Use the full legal institution name exactly as shown, including names shown in footer, copyright, disclosure, or legal text. Do not shorten to a logo or brand name when a fuller legal institution name appears. Example: return “Charles Schwab & Co., Inc.”, not “Charles Schwab".

Name of the account owner/customer shown on the bank statement. Use the full account title or registration as shown, including trustee, trust, U/A, FBO, or beneficiary wording when part of the account title. Do not return mailing addresses or bank names.
Account number shown on the statement. Return the exact displayed value, including masked or partial digits. Do not infer missing digits.
Statement date range or period covered by the bank statement. Use the exact dates shown.

Opening balance at the start of the statement period for the source cash/bank account. Use the exact amount shown; If no transaction-level running balance is shown, use the statement-level opening/starting cash balance and repeat it for each transaction from the same statement. Do not return Null only because the transaction row has no balance.

Closing balance at the end of the statement period for the source cash/bank account. Use the exact amount shown; If no transaction-level running balance is shown, use the statement-level closing/ending cash balance and repeat it for each transaction from the same statement. Do not return Null only because the transaction row has no balance.
Posted/effective date of the transaction. Use the date shown for that transaction.
Full transaction description exactly as shown, including merchant, payee, ID, card, or transfer details.
Transaction amount. Preserve debit/credit sign, negative value, parentheses, or withdrawal/deposit indicator as shown.

Assign the best short category from the transaction description. Use “fee” only when the description explicitly states fee, charge, service fee, or similar. Classify checks, check numbers, or “funds paid” transactions as check withdrawal/payment, not fee.
Return Yes only if the transaction is a payroll, employer, government, benefit, or ACH/PPD direct deposit credit. Otherwise return No.

Return Yes if the transaction is an outgoing withdrawal, debit, check/funds-paid transaction, Visa/card purchase, service/advisory fee, or transfer from an investment, brokerage, retirement, or securities account/institution. Do not require the description to explicitly say “investment.” Otherwise return No.
